sector_model: nonfinancial healthcare diagnostics (veterinary); GAAP earnings, FCF after capex, SBC shown, debt from credit facility plus senior notes, buyback-reduced equity
thesis: IDEXX (veterinary diagnostics; CAG Diagnostics recurring revenue about 80% of sales) reported Q3 2026 revenue +9.9% (organic +10.0%), comparable EPS 3.96 (+22%), 33.1% operating margin, and raised 2026 revenue (4,741-4,767M), EPS (14.96-15.16) and FCF conversion guidance. Stock closed 676.04 on 2026-11-06, up from 551.21 on 2026-10-30 (+22.6%). Market cap about 53.3B on 78.79M shares; TTM FCF 1.30B (2.4% yield), TTM net income 1.18B (45x). High quality, but price assumes continued double-digit growth.
counterthesis: Valuation is demanding: about 45x TTM GAAP earnings and 45x guided 2026 EPS midpoint, FCF yield 2.4% against a roughly 4% risk-free alternative, after a 22.6% one-week jump. Operating margin guidance was lowered (32.1-32.3% from 32.3-32.5%) because of the CoVet acquisition (about 250M, 230M goodwill, provisional). Debt rose to about 849M (credit facility 474M) as buybacks (810M in 9M26) exceed discretionary cash after acquisitions; 9M26 FCF 978M versus 810M repurchases plus 223M acquisition. Growth is largely vet-visit volume and price; companion animal visit softness (cf. Zoetis US companion animal -8% in the ZTS record) or pricing pushback could hit recurring revenue. Capital instrument revenue was flat. 10-Q appears internally inconsistent on the 3.72% senior notes (repaid vs 2027 series B listed). Litigation, MD&A and 10-K audit matters not read.
invalidation: Organic recurring revenue growth below 7% for two consecutive quarters; US clinical visit declines; operating margin under 30%; net debt/EBITDA above 1.5x from buybacks plus M&A; FCF falling below 90% of net income; CoVet integration charges or goodwill impairment.
